Jamaican Vibes Domino Rules

  • 4 players play with 7 dominoes each.
  • Choose Individual or Partner mode. In Partner mode, Player 1 & Player 3 play together against Player 2 & Player 4.
  • A domino must match one of the two open ends of the chain.
  • If your domino can play on either end, you choose which end to play.
  • If you have no legal play, the game automatically passes your turn.
  • The hand ends when a player plays their last domino or when the game becomes blocked.
  • In a blocked game, all remaining pips are counted. The player with the lowest pip total wins.
  • If a blocked game produces a tie across opposing sides, the next hand is worth 2 points and the player holding double-six (6–6) poses.
  • Timer: 10 seconds normally; 12 seconds when you have 3 dominoes left; 15 seconds when you have 2 dominoes left.
  • If the human player does not make a legal play before the timer expires, the game automatically plays a legal domino.
  • At the end of the hand, the remaining players' dominoes are revealed.
  • Bruck & Start (Partner Game): The first team to go 6 wins. A team starts by going 1, then 2, 3, and so on. If Team A is on 2 or more and Team B wins a hand, Team B brucks the run: the running score is cleared and the next hand starts again playing for 1. Special rule: if Team A goes 1 and Team B wins the next hand, it becomes one-one, and the next hand is ONE-ONE PLAY TWO. Whoever wins that hand goes 2. Example: A goes 1, B makes it one-one, then the next hand decides which team goes 2.
  • Offline play: The same Bruck & Start and ONE-ONE PLAY TWO partner rules are used against the computer. Online and offline partner scoring now match.
  • Disconnect / Reconnect: If an online player loses connection during an active game, the game pauses and that player has up to 90 seconds to reconnect to the same seat and hand.
  • Leaving / Forfeit: A player who deliberately leaves an active online match, or fails to reconnect within the allowed reconnect period, is treated as having left the match. The active match ends rather than allowing another person to take over the player's private hand.
  • Inactive Player (AFK): If a player does not make a move before the turn timer expires, the game may automatically make a legal play for that player. Repeated inactivity can be shown as inactive/AFK so the other players know the player is not responding.
  • Turn Timer: A player normally has 10 seconds to play. With 3 dominoes remaining the player has 12 seconds, and with 2 dominoes remaining the player has 15 seconds.
  • Automatic Pass: If a player has no legal domino, the game automatically passes that player's turn and continues to the next player.
  • Legal Moves: The server validates online moves. A domino must match a legal open end; a player cannot play a domino that is not in that player's hand or play on an illegal end.
  • Partner Poser: After a Partner hand is won, the winning team chooses which of its two partners will pose the next hand. The choice can be changed before it is confirmed.
  • Blocked Tie: If a blocked hand is tied across opposing sides, the next hand is worth 2 and the player holding double-six (6-6) poses.
  • Private Hands: During an active online hand, each player can see only their own hand. Other players' hands are revealed only when the hand is finished according to the game rules.
  • Room / Host: The room host selects the game mode and available match settings before play. Players must be connected and READY before an online match begins.
  • Host Fairness: A host may manage the room before the match starts, but active-game results and legal moves are controlled by the game server rather than by the host.
  • Match History: Online play keeps a game history showing important events such as plays, passes, hand wins, Brucks, One-One Play Two results, and the final match result.
  • Spectators: Spectators may watch supported online rooms but do not receive players' private hands while a hand is active and cannot make moves.
  • Rematch: After an online match finishes, all four players can vote for a rematch. A rematch resets the match score and starts a new Bruck and Start match.
